passage: Last year on the trip to the science park, my small bottle was empty by noon. My mouth felt like paper and I had to ask Hemant for sips, which made me feel bad. So this time I packed the big steel bottle. Amma said it was heavy, but I said I would rather be heavy than thirsty. I also told Hemant, "Bring a big one too, it gets really hot there." He laughed but agreed. At noon we sat in the shade, both bottles still half full, and I remembered last year and smiled. - Sonali

qa.q: Why did Sonali have to ask Hemant for sips last year?
qa.a: Sonali's small bottle was empty by noon.

qa.q: How did Sonali feel about asking Hemant for sips last year?
qa.a: Sonali felt bad and uncomfortable about it, and that memory pushed the change to a bigger bottle.

qa.q: What other approach could Sonali use to make sure water lasts through a hot day, and why?
qa.a: Sonali could ask the teacher where taps are on the route and top up there, so the day does not depend on one bottle.

qa.q: How might Hemant see Sonali's advice to bring a big bottle?
qa.a: He laughed, so it may seem a bit fussy at first, but at noon his bottle is half full too, which suggests the advice was sensible.

grounding: A child recalls being thirsty on last year's trip and changes the plan with a bigger bottle and a word to a friend.

subtype: Approach: learning from last year's trip and adjusting [Revision]
passage:
Class teacher's note, Class 5 picnic to the botanical park
On the bus this morning I noticed Binita holding a large steel bottle on her lap, nearly twice the size of the others. When I asked, she said, "Last year at the picnic my little bottle finished before lunch, and I was thirsty the whole afternoon. So this year I brought the big one." She had also told her friend Mahima to bring a bigger bottle, and Mahima had. By two o'clock, several children had empty bottles and were asking me for water. Binita and Mahima still had some left, and Binita shared a little with a boy who had none. I have added "one large water bottle" to next year's picnic notice.
- Class teacher

qa.q: What did Binita and Mahima still have at two o'clock?
qa.a: They still had some water left.

qa.q: How did Binita feel last year when her bottle ran out?
qa.a: She felt thirsty and uncomfortable the whole afternoon, which is why she remembered it.

qa.q: What else could Binita remember from last year's picnic to plan better?
qa.a: She could think about what else went wrong, like sun or tiredness, and add a cap or snack to her list.

qa.q: How does Binita's planning look to the class teacher?
qa.a: The teacher notices it and finds it useful enough to add a large bottle to next year's notice.

grounding: It shows a child remembering she was thirsty on last year's trip, carrying a bigger bottle this time and telling her friend to bring one too.

subtype: Approach: learning from last year's trip and adjusting [Revision]
passage:
Friday
Diary, today was the zoo trip, and I DIDN'T get thirsty. Last year my tiny pink bottle was empty by the lion cage, and I spent the whole afternoon with a dry mouth, watching others drink. So yesterday I asked Mummy for Papa's big blue bottle, the one he takes to work. It was heavy, but I put it in the side pocket. I also rang Yamini and told her, "Bring your biggest bottle, it gets really hot." She did. At lunch we sat under a tree and I still had half left. Yamini said, "You were right, Vasudha." I felt so clever. Next year I'm also bringing a cap, because my nose is red.
- Vasudha

qa.q: Whose bottle did Vasudha take on the zoo trip?
qa.a: Vasudha took Papa's big blue bottle.

qa.q: How did Vasudha feel when Yamini said "You were right"?
qa.a: Vasudha felt clever and proud that the plan worked for both of them.

qa.q: What else could Vasudha change for next year, and why?
qa.a: Vasudha plans to bring a cap because of the red nose, which shows how learning from each trip keeps improving the plan.

qa.q: How does the phone call look to Yamini?
qa.a: Yamini is glad of the warning, since the big bottle meant she had enough water too.

grounding: It shows a child remembering last year's thirst, bringing a bigger bottle and telling a friend to bring one too.
